story: Under the Consumer Protection Act 1986, how long do I have to complain? I paid Rs 12,000 for a course on 1 August 2026 and they cancelled it with no refund.

timeline.user_words: I paid Rs 12,000 for a course on 1 August 2026

timeline.event: Course was cancelled with no refund
timeline.user_words: they cancelled it with no refund

facts.user_goal: To know how long they have to complain under the Consumer Protection Act 1986 regarding a cancelled course with no refund

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 01 Aug 2028 (632 days left). This counts 2 years from 01 Aug 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 12,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You paid Rs 12,000 for a course that was cancelled. You can file a consumer complaint. You have until 01 Aug 2028 to file it. You should not wait. The course was bought for personal use, so it is covered. The complaint is free to file. You can file it where you live or work.

Not getting a refund for a cancelled course is an unfair trade practice.

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint because you bought the course for personal use.
support.reason: The law defines 'consumer' as someone who buys goods for consideration paid/promised, or hires/avails services for consideration paid/promised, and includes users with approval. The sentence states the person bought the course for personal use, which falls under buying goods/services for consideration, so the law supports this.

support.text: Not getting a refund for a cancelled course is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that refusing to refund consideration for deficient services 'within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days' is an unfair trade practice. Not getting a refund for a cancelled course falls under this.

support.text: You must file your complaint before 01 Aug 2028.
support.reason: The law text states the complaint must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose, not specifically by 01 Aug 2028. The sentence adds a specific date that is not in the law text and cannot be computed from the rule without knowing when the cause of action arose.

support.text: You do not have to pay a fee to file the complaint.
support.reason: The law text states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh' but also specifies fees for higher amounts (Rs 200 for above Rs 5 lakh to 10 lakh, etc.). The sentence states 'you do not have to pay a fee' without any condition, which is not supported as the fee depends on the amount paid.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the district where you live or work.
support.reason: The law text in s34(2)(d) explicitly states 'the complainant resides or personally works for gain' as a basis for filing in a District Commission, which directly supports the sentence.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the district where you live or work.
support.reason: The law text in s35(1) describes who can file a complaint (the consumer, recognised consumer association, one or more consumers, or government), not where the complaint can be filed. The sentence about filing in the district where you live or work is not supported by this law text.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 01 August 2026 I paid Rs 12,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 12,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: Payment of Rs 12,000 on 1 August 2026.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
